title: Jensen Huang will testify alone before the Senate on Dec. 3 about AI chip export controls
summary: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang will be the only witness at an open Senate Banking Committee hearing on U.S. export controls at 10 a.m. on Thursday, Dec. 3, in room 106 of the Dirksen Senate Office Building, Chip Dispatch reported on November 27, 2026. The hearing is titled “Protecting America’s AI Advantage: Oversight of U.S. Export Controls” and will stream live. Speaking on a Thanksgiving call with U.S. military personnel on Nov. 26, President Trump said Huang’s return would effectively begin Monday and called it “in a way, his second term,” adding, “the market feels very good about it.” Trump also said Nvidia’s Blackwell chip “will be obsolete in a year” and that Huang has “two new ones coming out that are blowing Blackwell away,” without naming them. Huang is also scheduled to meet House lawmakers privately next week, after three House Republican chairs sought a Dec. 1 transcribed interview. Chip Dispatch notes the hearing lands days after new U.S. rules pinched AI server shipments in Southeast Asia.

title: SAP is reportedly weighing at least 10,000 job cuts as it reshapes itself for AI
summary: German software giant SAP is preparing a plan to eliminate at least 10,000 positions as it reshapes its business for the artificial intelligence era, Bloomberg reported, according to CNBC on November 27, 2026. All departments were reportedly asked to identify potential cuts, with product, engineering and sales in particular focus; SAP employs more than 110,000 people. “The business environment in which we operate is changing rapidly through AI,” SAP said in a statement to CNBC, adding that “no decisions have been made regarding any further measures.” The company also flagged a cybersecurity incident but said it found “no evidence of unauthorized access to customer business data.” SAP cut around 10,000 positions in a 2024 reorganization and this year bought Reltio, Dremio, Prior Labs and TechWolf. U.S. employers cited AI in 121,401 job-cut announcements through October 2026, about 20% of the total, according to Challenger, Gray & Christmas.

title: Nvidia agrees to pay $290 million to end an eight-year lawsuit over crypto-mining GPU sales
summary: Nvidia has agreed to pay $290 million to settle an eight-year securities class action alleging it misled shareholders about how much cryptocurrency mining drove demand for its gaming GPUs in 2018, Chip Dispatch reported on November 27, 2026, citing Tom’s Hardware. The company did not admit wrongdoing, and a Tuesday court filing says the payment will be made in September. Investors alleged Nvidia counted mining demand as ordinary gaming sales; in November 2017 Jensen Huang described crypto’s contribution as “small but not zero.” After Nvidia cut guidance on Aug. 16, 2018, and acknowledged heavy mining use of GeForce cards, its shares fell 28.5% over two trading sessions. A district court dismissed the case in 2021, but the Ninth Circuit partly reversed that ruling and revived the claims. The settlement ends the suit without a court deciding whether the disclosures were misleading.

title: Belgium’s Wallonia orders Google to stop work at a nearly finished data center over a cooling-water fight
summary: Inspectors from Belgium’s Wallonia region gave about 300 workers a verbal stop order at Google’s Farciennes data center site on Thursday, Nov. 26, where a 30,000-square-meter building was nearly complete, Chip Dispatch reported on November 27, 2026. Google holds a 2024 permit for three air-cooled data centers on the 53-hectare site, but later sought to merge two buildings into one larger center cooled with water from the River Sambre; Walloon planning minister François Desquesnes refused that change in August, citing water demand. Google has appealed to Belgium’s Council of State, with a hearing set for Jan. 7. Greenpeace Belgium said satellite images showed construction continuing on Nov. 25 and filed an urgent complaint a day before the inspection. Google told RTBF it was “committed to an open and collaborative dialogue” with the regional government. The order follows a Nov. 24 Virginia ruling that voided a county approval for another Google data center.

title: Texas reopens its permit queue for more than 1,800 stalled data-center projects
summary: Texas has resumed approvals for more than 1,800 data-center projects that outgoing Gov. Greg Abbott’s office put on hold in August, when a moratorium covered 474 gigawatts of new power requests, Chip Dispatch reported on November 27, 2026. Chip Dispatch stresses that the 474 GW figure counts power applications, not operating computing capacity. The pause was tied to grid strain; Abbott’s office said its “top priority is to protect Texans’ safety and quality of life.” Reviews restarted after the state grid operator ERCOT finished gathering information on data centers’ effects on local communities. The Financial Times reported that builders are racing to secure approvals before Democrat Gina Hinojosa takes office in January, after she pledged to rein in new data-center construction. Some developers are pursuing their own gas-turbine power to reduce reliance on the grid. No processing schedule or project list accompanied the directive.

title: S&P 500 futures jump about 2% into a half-day session as Wall Street heads for its best week since April 2025
summary: Stock futures rose ahead of Friday’s holiday-shortened session, with S&P 500 futures up nearly 2%, Nasdaq-100 futures up 2.3% and Dow futures higher by around 1%, CNBC’s Morning Squawk reported on November 27, 2026, as investors bought the dip in the biggest AI names. Nvidia was up over 4% in premarket trading, alongside Anthropic, Alphabet, Amazon and Microsoft. Entering Friday, the S&P 500 was up 3.9% for the week and the Nasdaq 4.1%, while the Dow’s 4.2% gain put it on pace for its biggest weekly advance since April 2025, CNBC’s live updates said. The market was closed Thursday for Thanksgiving and closes at 1 p.m. ET (noon Central) on Friday. Traders are pricing a near-100% chance of a rate hike at the Fed’s December meeting after third-quarter GDP was revised up to 4.3% annualized from 3.4%. Chip Dispatch, citing Reuters, notes the S&P 500 and Nasdaq are still on track for their worst November since 2008.

title: Cambricon jumps 18.68% as Chinese chip stocks post their biggest one-day gain on record
summary: AI chipmaker Cambricon rose 18.68% to 1,118.99 yuan on Friday, Nov. 27, as China’s CSI Semiconductor Industry Index closed 17.60% higher at 6,685.06, its largest one-day gain on record, Chip Dispatch reported on November 27, 2026, citing Wind data. Hygon Information Technology gained 18.05%, SMIC rose 15.38% to 134.42 yuan in Shanghai, and Hua Hong Semiconductor closed up 20.00%. The STAR 50 gained 15.07% and the CSI 300 4.17%. The rally followed a State Council meeting chaired by Premier Li Qiang that pledged to strengthen the role of the state-backed “national team” and Central Huijin in stabilizing markets; CNBC reported the readout was released during trading hours, an unusual timing investors read as bullish. “Stock market performance is now prioritized at the highest level for the Chinese government,” Shanghai venture capitalist Bob Chen told CNBC. Chip Dispatch notes UBS forecasts Chinese suppliers will take 88% of China’s AI processor market by 2028.

title: ASML climbs 4.67% as European chipmakers ride China’s record rally
summary: ASML rose 4.67% to €1,222.80 at about 12:19 p.m. CET on Friday, Nov. 27, as chipmakers and miners lifted Europe’s Stoxx 600 0.98% to 643.25, Chip Dispatch reported on November 27, 2026, citing CNBC market data. Technology was Europe’s strongest sector, up 2.6% in the morning, according to Investing.com; ASM International gained 4.52%, Infineon 4.12%, BE Semiconductor 4.08%, Soitec 5.56% and STMicroelectronics 3.69%. The trigger came from China, where the CSI Semiconductor index posted its biggest one-day rise on record after a State Council pledge to support the stock market. Chip Dispatch cautions that it was an equity-market catalyst, with no new orders, capacity or pricing figures behind it. French laser maker Lumibird jumped 17.72% after Thales began exclusive talks to take control. “There doesn’t seem to be any firm catalyst behind the bounce that we’ve seen,” StoneX analyst Fiona Cincotta said.

title: SpaceX shares jump 4% in premarket trading amid the tech rally and Musk’s new share-donation pledge
summary: SpaceX shares rose 4% in premarket trading on Friday amid a broader tech rally and after Elon Musk expanded his share-donation plan for American children, CNBC reported on November 27, 2026. “I will be donating another share of SpaceX to all kids in America every year,” Musk posted on X. The stock had jumped more than 7% in overnight trading on Blue Ocean ATS, which resumed at 8 p.m. ET on Thanksgiving Day, after closing up 1.30% on Wednesday. On Wednesday SpaceX said it would donate one Class A share to every active Trump Account, the tax-advantaged investment accounts for American children, with Musk personally matching the gift; Musk said SpaceX’s contribution would be transferred next month and his own after his lockup expires next June. Nearly 70 million Trump Accounts had been created as of October, according to the White House. Nvidia, Intel, Marvell, AMD and Micron were also higher before the bell.

title: PrismML’s Ternary Bonsai 2.5 packs a 27B coding model into about 5.9 GB of open weights
summary: PrismML introduced Ternary Bonsai 2.5 27B on November 24, an upgrade to its compressed open-weight language model, Open Model Weights reported on November 26, 2026. Built on Qwen3.8-27B, it keeps a ternary representation: the GGUF model card lists an effective 1.76 bits per weight and a 5.93 GB packing, against 53.8 GB for the FP16 reference. PrismML reports SWE-bench Verified improving from 60.8 to 75.6 and AppWorld from 51.2 to 90.5 versus Bonsai 2 — publisher evaluations, not independent measurements. The weights are released under Apache 2.0 with GGUF and MLX options; the most compact packing needs PrismML’s llama.cpp fork, while a Q2_0 version runs on upstream llama.cpp, and optional multi-token prediction variants add a draft head for speculative decoding. Open Model Weights cautions that weight file size is not total runtime memory, since context length and cache also count.

title: Aleph Alpha’s Kolibri 1.1 says it cuts GPU time per task about 3.4-fold for German and English work
summary: German developer Aleph Alpha released Kolibri 1.1 on November 23, roughly seven weeks after the first Kolibri, Open Model Weights reported on November 26, 2026. The open-weight mixture-of-experts reasoning model has roughly 75 billion total parameters and around 3.4 billion active per token, adds sparse attention, and is released under Apache 2.0. Aleph Alpha reports a roughly 3.4-fold reduction in GPU time per task versus the original Kolibri and 41% fewer generated output tokens on average; its technical report lists an aggregate score of 73.2 and 0.208 GPU-hours per 1,000 evaluation tasks. Open Model Weights notes these are publisher results, not independently reproduced benchmarks, and that a model license alone does not guarantee compliance with European privacy rules. It calls the focus on efficiency per completed task, rather than raw token speed, the release’s most interesting feature.

title: MemTensor opens MemT-1.0-Pro, a 554B-parameter model that builds memory into the model itself
summary: MemTensor announced MemT-1.0-Pro on November 23, a memory-native model developed in collaboration with Nvidia and built on Nemotron 3 Ultra, Open Model Weights reported on November 25, 2026. Instead of relying only on an external store of past conversations, it tries to make memory part of the model’s computation. The publisher reports about 554 billion parameters overall and 59 billion active, plus 4.23 billion trainable memory parameters and a 13-million-parameter dynamic memory state. The checkpoint is listed on Hugging Face under the OpenMDW-1.1 license, while the project’s SGLang serving code carries a PolyForm Noncommercial license, so access to the weights is not the same as unrestricted commercial deployment. Open Model Weights says the approach raises new questions for long-running agents, such as how stored facts are updated, audited or removed, and that the benchmark results remain publisher-reported.

title: Europe’s largest satellite factory opens in Belgium, built to turn out up to 500 satellites a year
summary: The largest satellite factory in Europe was inaugurated in Belgium this week by King Philippe, boosting the continent’s push to challenge Elon Musk’s Starlink, CNBC reported on November 26, 2026. Belgian manufacturer Aerospacelab, which will be renamed Ectro from Nov. 30, won a €2.4 billion ($2.6 billion) contract in September to build 264 of the 348 satellites planned for IRIS², the European Union’s secure-connectivity constellation. Its oval-shaped, 20,000-square-meter facility in southern Belgium will be able to produce up to 500 satellites a year, which would make it the world’s third-largest satellite production site, according to the Belgian royal palace. Employees are expected to move in in January, with production slated to begin by the end of 2028, according to AFP. SpaceX says it has more than 11,000 Starlink satellites in low Earth orbit; IRIS² aims for first launches by the end of 2029.

title: Kyocera bets its next five years on AI data-center parts, targeting ¥2.6 trillion in sales
summary: Kyocera has set a target of ¥2.6 trillion in sales and ¥320 billion in operating profit for the fiscal year ending March 2031, a plan built largely on parts for AI data centers and optical networks, Chip Dispatch reported on November 27, 2026. The company presented the figures at a business strategy meeting on Nov. 26; fiscal 2026 sales were ¥2,070.2 billion with operating profit of ¥118.1 billion. Its largest growth driver, parts for AI network infrastructure — ceramic packages for data-center optical links, capacitors for AI servers and packages for optical switches — is planned to grow from ¥86.0 billion to about ¥310 billion, a 29% annual rate. Kyocera estimates it holds more than 90% of the market for ceramic packages used in inter-data-center and backbone optical communications. Over five years it plans ¥900 billion of capital spending, ¥650 billion for R&D and ¥850 billion for acquisitions or buybacks.

title: Sony spin-off Altair raises $100 million to mass-produce a low-power 5G modem for AI glasses and wearables
summary: Altair Semiconductor, spun out of Sony in April, raised a $100 million Series A led by Maverick Silicon to mass-produce its ALT1550 low-power 5G modem for smart glasses and wearables, with production scheduled for 2027, Chip Dispatch reported on November 26, 2026, citing CTech by Calcalist. Israeli venture firm Pitango also took part; no valuation was disclosed. The chip combines 5G eRedCap — a stripped-down 5G feature for low-data, long-battery devices — with 4G Cat 1bis, LTE-M and satellite connectivity. On Nov. 19, Ericsson and Altair said they had completed the first eRedCap network connection using the ALT1550. “AI is about to go everywhere we go, and every one of those devices needs a connection that is always on,” CEO Nohik Semel told CTech, adding that “demand for ALT1550 is ahead of plan.” Chip Dispatch notes Altair has not named customers, volumes or revenue.

title: After 37 years of Thanksgiving dinners for 2,000 neighbors, a Texas town buys ‘Miss Gloria’ a new car
summary: For 37 years Gloria Kennard has cooked Thanksgiving dinner for her Texas community — a tradition she began in 1988 that now feeds more than 2,000 people — and this year the town returned the kindness, Good News Network reported on November 26, 2026. After a July crash totaled her truck and the insurance payout fell short, The Bridge Ministries food pantry, where she has volunteered weekly for 16 years, launched a GoFundMe with a $15,000 goal. By October, 174 donors had given more than $17,700, and local business Kent Moore Cabinets added $10,000, pushing the total above $27,000. Friends surprised her on Oct. 30 with a new Kia SUV. “Miss Gloria is always giving her heart away to people,” said The Bridge Ministries’ Emma Bridges. “And so we have to do the same to her.” Kennard’s reply: “Thank you so very much, community. And God bless you.”

title: For this New York restaurant owner, Thanksgiving comes every Wednesday
summary: Every Wednesday night for the past five years, Ali Riza Dogan, owner of Ali Baba Mediterranean & Turkish Cuisine in Midtown Manhattan, has loaded catering pans with hot food and driven to Chinatown to serve free meals to 100 to 150 people who are homeless or struggling, Good News Network reported on November 26, 2026. On Thanksgiving eve he brought plenty of turkey, joined by community volunteers. The routine traces back to a night years ago when, newly arrived from Turkey and working as a dishwasher, he got lost, spoke little English and spent a cold night hungry in a hallway. “We never forget where we come from,” he said. When it turns cold, he leaves the heat running in his restaurant’s entryway with a sign welcoming anyone who needs a warm place to rest. “Maybe we cannot change the whole world, but if we can help even one person sleep warmer, then we have done something meaningful.”

title: A baby given weeks to live on Christmas Eve is now a cancer-free 7-year-old
summary: Seven years ago, a newborn named Imani was diagnosed with an aggressive high-grade glioma and her parents, both physicians, were told she had weeks to live, Good News Network reported on November 26, 2026. They sent her records to 15 hospitals worldwide and heard the same answer, until St. Jude Children’s Research Hospital, which had just finished a clinical trial on her form of cancer, called on Christmas Eve as they pulled onto their street in Dix Hills, New York. “We went from the lowest point to the highest point in a matter of minutes,” mother Sarah Syed told Patch. After two cycles of experimental chemotherapy shrank the tumor by about 50%, a March 2020 surgery removed it; the surgeon’s words were, “I got it all.” Today Imani is cancer-free, loves gymnastics, swimming and piano, and for her 7th birthday asked for donations to St. Jude instead of gifts.

title: Holiday lights are on: Christmas at Bridge Point’s drive-through display is open Friday through Sunday nights
summary: Christmas at Bridge Point, a drive-through Christmas light display at 7200 Johnston St. in Lafayette, opened Thanksgiving night for its fifth year and runs through December 23, Macaroni KID Lafayette reported. Lights shine from 6 to 10 p.m. Wednesday through Sunday, so it is open tonight, Saturday and Sunday; it is closed Mondays and Tuesdays. Admission is per vehicle: $25 for cars, $40 for vans and $100 for buses and trolleys, with tickets available online or at the gate. The Lafayette Mom describes more than half a million lights across 24 acres on Lafayette’s Southside, with light tunnels that are a favorite for kids. The bigger light shows come later: Noël Acadien au Village at LARC’s Acadian Village opens Dec. 1.

title: Santa’s Sleigh rides and a Christmas tree lighting come to South College Center on Saturday
summary: South College Center, 2801–2851 Johnston St., hosts free Santa’s Sleigh rides and holiday shopping on Saturday, November 28, from noon to 5:30 p.m., with its annual Christmas Tree Lighting at dusk, according to the event listing. Santa’s Sleigh runs from noon to 5 p.m. Saturday. Saturday’s free activities include face painting and glitter tattoos, letter writing to Santa, a DIY reindeer food bar, Christmas card making, ornament decorating, photos and storytime with Mrs. Claus, live youth entertainment by Wonderland Performing Arts and a Christmas photo station. The sleigh returns on Saturdays, December 5, 12 and 19, from 10 a.m. to noon and 1 to 3 p.m.

title: Free basketball Sunday: the Ragin’ Cajuns women host Jackson State at the Cajundome
summary: Louisiana’s women’s basketball team hosts Jackson State at the Cajundome at 4 p.m. on Sunday, November 29, according to the Ragin’ Cajuns game center, with coverage on ESPN+ and KPEL 96.5 FM. Admission is free, the Cajundome’s event page says, and doors open an hour before tipoff. The Cajundome’s clear-bag policy is in effect, with general parking at the Cajundome, no outside food or drink, no re-entry and cashless concessions. Jackson State won the teams’ last meeting, 70–41, on Nov. 16, 2022, the game center shows.

title: Louisiana Christmas Day gala opens the holiday season at the Heymann on Sunday
summary: Bayou Teche Music Productions presents “Louisiana Christmas Day: 5th Anniversary Gala” this Sunday, November 29, featuring bass-baritone André Courville and the Atchafalaya Orchestra with special guests Sweet Cecilia, Wayne Toups, Chubby Carrier, Jennifer Kaye, Jourdan Thibodeaux and Hunter Courville, Acadiana Profile reported in its Nov. 27–29 weekend guide. The concert starts at 6 p.m. at the Heymann Performing Arts Center, 1373 South College Road, according to Sweet Cecilia’s event listing. The same guide lists the Turkey Day Classic in The Boot, a dance competition bringing teams from across the country to the George Dupuis Recreation Center this weekend.
